fullPassage: "Art without commerce is a hobby." These words, spoken with much authority to several hundred students at the first of a series of "Art Talk" lectures, completely rocked my world. For the first time in my life, I had to face the fact that what I was doing was a hobby. As a kid I used to draw endlessly, using ink, acrylic, and even spray cans. But I never once thought about making a dollar from my art. Over the years, this approach of "creating for creation's sake" was reinforced by people around me, including school teachers, who would say things like, "Draw whatever your heart desires." So by the time I graduated from college, I had convinced myself that having a career in the arts meant working in a bubble, creating what I wanted to create and then hoping the world would like it. But the cold reality was that almost no one was interested in my art because it had no _______________.

For the first time in my life, I had to face the fact that what I was doing was a hobby. As a kid I used to draw endlessly, ③<u>using</u> ink, acrylic, and even spray cans. But I never once thought about making a dollar from my art. Over the years, this approach of "creating for creation's sake" was reinforced by people around me, including school teachers, who would ④<u>saying</u> things like, "Draw whatever your heart desires." So by the time I graduated from college, I had convinced myself that having a career in the arts meant working in a bubble, creating what I wanted to create and then ①<u>hoping</u> the world would like it. But the cold reality was that almost no one was interested in my art because it had no _______________.

det.korean: saying → say: 'who would say things like'에서 would 뒤에 동사원형 say 필요
det.analysis:
① rocked — 과거형 동사로 주어 These words에 대한 동사, 정상 ←오답
② using — 분사구문으로 수단을 나타냄, 정상 ←오답
③ saying — 'who would saying things'에서 조동사 would 뒤에 동사원형 say 필요, saying은 비문 ←정답
④ hoping — 'creating... and then hoping'에서 병렬 동명사, 정상 ←오답
det.tip: 'would + 동사원형' 구조에서 would 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 와야 합니다. would saying은 문법적으로 틀립니다.
